newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian bonds press against resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian bonds press against resistance.

text.p: *Australian bond futures extended Tuesday's sharp rally in after hours trading after U.S. Treasuries surged on a weaker than feared March CPI report.
*Local bond contracts pressing against key support levels of 92.120 on the 10-year and 93.12 on the three year.
Australian bond futures extended Tuesday's sharp rally in after hours trading as U.S. Treasuries surged on a weaker-than-feared March CPI report on Tuesday.
The June 10-year bond futures contract ended SYCOM trading at its highest level in a month at 92.120, compared with Tuesday's 92.035 close, and after slicing through resistance at 92.050 and 92.080.

However, the 92.120 level could prove stiff resistance, representing a 38.2 percent retracement of the mid-February to early April sell-off from 92.760 to 91.700, and given that the contract has put on nearly 25 basis points since Monday.
On the downside, initial support is expected at 92.080, the contract's previous recent peak seen last Thursday following the weaker than expected labour force report.

The local market made a strong outperformance against the U.S. on Tuesday in a continued realisation that the Reserve Bank will at the very least keep policy on hold for some months to come, and may even need to ease again if the forthcoming data flow is benign, to keep the recovery in motion.
U.S. Treasury yields dropped on Tuesday on a short covering rally sparked by modest increases in both headline and core CPI of respectively 0.1 and 0.2 percent and below expectations.
However, despite the relief from the data, it has not changed the general view that the Federal Reserve will be tightening policy again.
The local market sees its own quarterly CPI report next Wednesday.
Meanwhile, the Westpac consumer sentiment survey for April is due at 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).
